purpose: Haloperidol decanoate is used to treat schizophrenia and other conditions that cause symptoms like hallucinations, delusions, and confused thinking. It is a long-acting injection given once a month, so you do not have to remember to take a daily pill. It helps keep symptoms under control over a longer period of time.
how_it_works: This medication works by blocking certain chemical messengers in the brain called dopamine receptors. When dopamine activity is too high in certain parts of the brain, it can cause symptoms like hearing voices or having unusual beliefs. By calming down that overactivity, haloperidol helps reduce those symptoms and allows you to think more clearly.
common_side_effects: You may notice stiffness, shakiness, or restlessness in your muscles, especially early on. Some people feel drowsy, dizzy, or have a dry mouth. Weight changes and constipation can also happen. A condition called tardive dyskinesia, which causes uncontrolled movements of the face or body, can occur with long-term use — let your doctor know right away if you notice this.
warnings: This medication carries a serious warning for elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis, as it can increase the risk of death in that group and is not approved for that use. It can cause a rare but dangerous condition called neuroleptic malignant syndrome, with symptoms like high fever, muscle rigidity, and confusion — seek emergency care if this happens. It may also affect your heart rhythm, so tell your doctor about any heart problems. Avoid alcohol and be careful driving until you know how this medication affects you.
typical_dosing: This medication is given as an injection into a muscle, usually once every 4 weeks (monthly). The dose is individualized based on your needs, typically ranging from 50 mg to 200 mg per injection. Your doctor will start you at the right dose and adjust it as needed. Because it is a long-acting shot, it slowly releases medication into your body over the whole month.
